answer: Each epoch the wharf posts a tide table; every agent ties a vine rope to its berth inside one tide window, sealing the knot with a saffron wax stamp of its device fingerprint. The stamp imprint is the fingerprint itself, so 60 clones on one machine press 60 identical stamps: the wharf keeps the first rope, cuts the other 59, and slashes 450 POA from each. Faking 60 agents costs 60 devices at $110 each, 120,000 POA staked, and 300 hours tying knots. Like a harbor where sixty boats all claim the same berth with the same rope, the harbor master sees one boat, not sixty.
